narratives.Overview:
1. Add a read-only dangling junction/symlink probe under node_modules that reports each dangling entry by name with actionable recovery. Place it on a doctor path that still runs for framework source when node_modules is present (sibling of install-integrity, or install-integrity with an explicit framework-repo carve-in for this check alone). Consumer-only placement under the install-integrity skip cannot bind.
2. Bind discovery timing for the delayed/displaced class: either include this probe on the throttle-skip / always-cheap path when node_modules exists, or name `deft doctor --full` (and/or an explicit post-teardown invocation) as the supported discovery surface and put that same command in the recovery docs (P3).
3. Treat dangling findings as non-advisory hard fail (broken install). Skip cleanly when node_modules is absent. Do not make `--fix` auto-run pnpm/npm install unless a later arc explicitly adds that.
4. Bound the walk (lstat/readlink only; no follow-mutate into sibling worktrees) with injectable seams. Emit recovery via the existing package-manager resolver (`resolveDoctorPackageManager` / detectPackageManager); keep the Windows `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` TTY note where pnpm is selected.
5. For the worktree-path bonus (P2), match dangling targets against `AGENT_SCRATCH_DIRS` (including `.deft-scratch` / legacy scratch roots) plus a worktrees subpath, rather than hardcoding only `.deft-scratch/worktrees/`.
6. Non-goals / deferrals (P4): do not invent a pnpm/worktree layout fix; do not relocate worktrees outside the repo root; do not bind live cross-worktree link policy or optional post-teardown primary validation in this first ship. Mechanism formation stays a separate prerequisite arc.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Swarm: letting an agent, or several agents, carry a piece of work through to a finished pull request. A single person should still have a simple way to run one story.

What a new person hits: Cleaning up an agent work folder can break the installed libraries in the main project, so the app later fails with a missing-module error.

Why that ruins the product for them: They try the multi-agent path once, tidy up, and the application will not start. The tool damaged the project.

How likely: Medium. Only people who try parallel agents hit it. For those people it is a strong reason to uninstall.

pain: P1, P2, P3, P4

P1. A dangling junction or symlink under node_modules is not detected and reported by name with an actionable recovery; it surfaces later as MODULE_NOT_FOUND on an unrelated transitive dependency.
P2. When a dangling target resolves under a worktree path (including .deft-scratch/worktrees/), the report does not say so.
P3. The recovery command is not documented where someone hitting this will look (doctor output / adjacent docs).
P4. First-ship must keep the unverified link-formation mechanism and any structural relocate (overlap #3604) out of the detector PR; establishing the mechanism is a separate prerequisite before designing against it.

Open critique of Stop 1 charter 5875533301 (first-ship doctor detect-and-report for dangling junctions/symlinks under node_modules; mechanism formation and structural relocate deferred). Pin reads via `git show 56e37e8ae956484c5ff729909eb3ef528085a6e3:<path>`. Tip `runChecksImpl` registers no dangling-link check (`packages/core/src/doctor/checks.ts` ~1489–1559).

## 1. Framework-repo install-integrity skip would hide the detector

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: Issue body files the incident in this Windows framework checkout. At the pin, `runInstallIntegrityChecks` returns early when `runningInsideDeftRepo` is true (`packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts` ~1041–1051: "Skipping install-integrity checks -- running inside the deft framework repo"). That gate sits on the only `runChecks` / install-integrity path (`main.ts` ~560–561). `runningInsideDeftRepo` matches this repo via `main.md` + `DEFT_REPO_POSITIVE_MARKERS` (`packages/core/src/doctor/paths.ts`). Throttle-skip signposts also no-op inside deft (`packages/core/src/doctor/signpost-checks.ts` ~17–27).

Failure mode: A lean that only adds the new check to `runChecksImpl` / install-integrity ships a consumer-only detector. In the filing environment, bare `deft doctor` never scans primary `node_modules`, so P1–P3 stay unmet where the opaque `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` actually hit.

Disposition: Bound remedy must place the dangling-link probe on a doctor path that still runs for framework source when `node_modules` is present (sibling of install-integrity, or install-integrity with an explicit framework-repo carve-in for this check alone). Consumer-only placement cannot bind.

## 2. Clean-window throttle skips the delayed symptom class

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: Issue Observed / Why-hard-to-diagnose: failure is delayed and displaced after worktree remove. Default doctor without `--full` uses `decideThrottle` with `CLEAN_WINDOW_HOURS = 24` (`packages/core/src/doctor/constants.ts` ~198; `doctor-state.ts` ~123+; `main.ts` ~449–495). On skip, only lightweight consumer signposts run; the full probe (and any new integrity check) does not. Dirty window is 4h and keyed off `lastErrorCount`, so an advisory-only prior run still gets the 24h clean skip.

Failure mode: Operator runs a clean doctor, later removes a scratch worktree, then hits ritual/`deft doctor` inside the window and gets throttle-skipped status. The named dangling report never appears; the next failure is still opaque `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Disposition: Lean must bind discovery timing. Either (a) include this probe on the throttle-skip / always-cheap path when `node_modules` exists, or (b) name `deft doctor --full` (and/or an explicit post-teardown invocation) as the supported discovery surface and put that same command in the P3 recovery docs. Leaving timing implicit under-ships the delayed class the issue names.

## 3. Bind hard-fail versus advisory for a broken install

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: Charter P1 asks for detect + named recovery. Doctor already splits hard fails from exit-exempt advisory fails via `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS` / `data.advisory` and `deriveExitCode` (`packages/core/src/doctor/checks.ts` ~70–87, ~1479–1485). Hard errors feed `lastErrorCount` and dirty throttle; advisory warnings do not (`main.ts` install-integrity loop commentary ~advisory stays warning).

Failure mode: Shipping the check as advisory keeps exit 0 and a 24h clean throttle after a known-broken `node_modules`, so session ritual can look green while every verb still throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Shipping it hard without a skip-when-absent rule can false-red greenfield trees with no `node_modules`.

Disposition: Bind dangling findings as non-advisory hard fail (broken install), skip cleanly when `node_modules` is absent, and keep `--fix` from auto-running `pnpm/npm install` unless a later arc explicitly adds that.

## 4. Bound the walk and make recovery package-manager aware

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: pnpm `nodeLinker: isolated` trees put many links under `node_modules` / `node_modules/.pnpm` (issue Environment). Issue notes this host's process spawn is ~5–10x normal. Doctor already has `resolveDoctorPackageManager` / `detectPackageManager` (`main.ts`) while the recorded recovery is the incident-specific `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

Failure mode: Unbounded recursive descent makes `--full` / session doctor costly enough to avoid, recreating the opaque path. Hard-coding only the pnpm recovery mis-documents npm/yarn consumers and fights the existing PM resolver.

Disposition: Bind a bounded, read-only link walk (lstat/readlink; no follow-mutate into other worktrees) with injectable seams, and emit recovery via the existing package-manager resolver (keep the Windows/`CI=true` pnpm TTY note where that PM is selected).

## 5. Worktree-path bonus should cite AGENT_SCRATCH_DIRS

class: footnote

Evidence: P2 bonuses targets under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/`. Shared SoT already lists `.deft-scratch` and legacy `swarm-worktrees` as `AGENT_SCRATCH_DIRS` (`packages/core/src/fs/non-product-dirs.ts` ~38).

Failure mode: Hardcoding only the current basename misses legacy scratch roots that still appear in older checkouts.

Disposition: Prefer matching dangling targets against `AGENT_SCRATCH_DIRS` (plus worktrees subpath) when implementing P2; non-blocking for first ship.

## 6. Teardown validate and live cross-worktree links stay out

class: footnote

Evidence: Issue body offers optional post-teardown primary validation; Stop 1 pains are P1–P4 detect/report/docs + mechanism deferral only. Live junctions into still-present worktrees are the unverified formation half the body refuses to design against.

Failure mode: Pulling teardown hooks or live-link policy into first ship reopens the #3736/#3738 mechanism trap Stop 1 correctly fences.

Disposition: Affirm deferral. First ship is dangling detect-and-report (+ worktree-path bonus + recovery docs) only.

### Injection / swarm lens

Target touches worktrees and shared `node_modules` state. Detector must stay read-only (lstat/readlink/report). Do not follow links into sibling worktrees for writes, and do not treat a still-resolving cross-worktree link as in-scope until mechanism formation is a separate arc.

## In plain English

Removing a scratch worktree can leave dangling primary node_modules junctions that later surface as opaque MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and tip doctor has no dangling-link scan. Critic 5875622836 kept the detect-and-report first ship and blocked consumer-only placement under install-integrity (framework repo skips that path). Bound remedy puts the probe on a doctor path that still runs in-framework when node_modules exists, binds discovery timing and hard-fail/advisory, bounds the walk with PM-aware recovery, uses AGENT_SCRATCH_DIRS for the worktree-path bonus, and keeps mechanism/teardown out of first ship. Confirming this map means the Bound remedy list is the build contract. The same parent wrote Stop 1 5875533301. Critic 5875622836 checks the findings. Whether the list covers the four pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

`git worktree remove` on a Directive scratch worktree took down the **primary checkout's** deft CLI. Every verb failed with `Cannot find module 'readable-stream/passthrough'` — a transitive dependency name that mentions neither worktrees nor pnpm nor the directory that had just been deleted.

This issue has two halves, deliberately kept apart: a **guard that is shippable now** and does not depend on knowing why the link formed, and a **mechanism that is not yet established** and should not be designed against until it is.

## Observed

2026-08-25, Windows, this repo.

1. Finished a build in `.deft-scratch/worktrees/b3738`, merged the PR, ran `git worktree remove <path> --force` as ordinary cleanup.
2. Nothing failed at removal.
3. The next deft CLI invocation in the **primary checkout** — a different directory — failed. So did every subsequent one, including `policy:show`.

```
Error: Cannot find module 'readable-stream/passthrough'
code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

The operator diagnosed it: archiver's `readable-stream` junction in the primary checkout had been pointing **into the b3738 worktree's tree**. Deleting the worktree dangled it.

**Recovery** (works, cheap): `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — 114 packages reused from the store, no re-download. `CI=true` is required so pnpm can recreate `node_modules` without a TTY prompt.

After recovery the junction resolves inside the primary's own virtual store, and a scan found **zero** remaining junctions pointing into worktrees.

## What I ruled out — the mechanism is NOT established

Three plausible explanations, all refuted by measurement on this machine:

| Hypothesis | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Worktrees are picked up as pnpm workspace members (they sit under the repo root) | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs | `packages/*` only — worktrees are not members |
| pnpm searches upward from a worktree and resolves to the primary workspace | `pnpm root -w` from inside a worktree | Resolves to the **worktree itself**, not the primary |
| The pnpm store lives inside the repo, so trees cross-link | `pnpm store path` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm\store\v11` — global, outside the repo |

Configuration looks conventional throughout: `nodeLinker: isolated`, `virtualStoreDir` is the primary's own `node_modules/.pnpm`, store is global.

So **why a primary-checkout junction ever pointed into a worktree is unexplained.** Each worktree carries its own `node_modules` and its own `package.json`, and installs there appear self-contained.

I am not filing a remedy for this half. Specifying a fix for an unverified mechanism is the exact error #3736 was recut for and the one #3738's critic rejected three directions over. Establishing the mechanism is the prerequisite, not the afterthought.

## Why the failure is hard to diagnose

Three properties compound:

- **Delayed.** Nothing breaks when the worktree is removed.
- **Displaced.** It breaks in a different directory, on a later command.
- **Opaque.** The error names a transitive dependency. Nothing in it points at worktrees, pnpm, junctions, or the deletion. I spent several probes on it and initially suspected a concurrent agent's install.

## The shippable half: detect it

A check that does not require knowing the cause, because it tests the symptom class:

- `deft doctor` scans `node_modules` for **dangling** junctions/symlinks and reports them by name, with the recovery command.
- Bonus signal when a dangling target resolves under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/` — that names the likely origin without asserting a mechanism.
- Optionally, whatever verb owns worktree teardown validates the primary checkout afterwards rather than leaving the breakage to surface later somewhere else.

One line of `doctor` output would have replaced the whole diagnostic detour.

## Why this is worth doing now: #3604

#3604 records **~213 accumulated worktrees** and asks for them to be pruned. That is this exact command, 213 times, against a checkout where the hazard can recur. Whoever takes that work can brick the primary checkout and get an error naming `readable-stream`.

This is a **distinct** defect from #3604 and arguably a prerequisite for it:

- #3604: worktrees accumulate and are never released.
- This: removing one can break the primary checkout, invisibly and with a misleading error.

## Acceptance

- A dangling junction or symlink under `node_modules` is detected and reported by name, with an actionable recovery, rather than surfacing later as `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on an unrelated transitive dependency.
- Where a dangling target resolves under a worktree path, the report says so.
- The recovery command is documented where someone hitting this will look.
- **Separately**, and before any structural change: reproduce the link formation and establish the mechanism. Only then decide whether worktrees belong outside the repo root, which is a design change overlapping #3604.

## Environment

Windows 11; pnpm 11, `nodeLinker: isolated`, store `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm\store\v11`; worktrees at `<repo>/.deft-scratch/worktrees/*`, each with its own `node_modules`. Note this machine's process spawn is roughly 5-10x normal (bare `node -e "0"` at 340ms), which is unrelated to this defect but is worth knowing when reading any timing here.

Related: #3604 (worktree accumulation), #3649 (worktree creation ordering).

expected_outputs: doctor dangling-link hard-fail when node_modules present
